247159795_fb7a534b.text: The intergeniculate leaflet (IGL) and ventral lateral geniculate nucleus (LGv) are visual nuclei within the lateral geniculate complex of the mouse thalamus that are composed almost exclusively of GABAergic projection neurons. These neurons receive direct retinal input and extend projections to numerous subcortical visual and nonvisual targets, including visual structures, vestibular nuclei, and nuclei involved in circadian behavior and eye movements (Harrington, 1997; Morin and Blanchard, 2001; Morin and Allen, 2006; Seabrook et al., 2017)
247159795_fb7a534b.section: Connectivity and circuit function of vLGN GABAergic neurons

247159795_aeeef91c.text: .During embryogenesis, dLGN and IGL/ LGv arise from separate developmental domains, the pTH-C and pTH-R domains, respectively (Vue et al., 2007; Nakagawa and O’Leary, 2001; Suzuki-Hirano et al., 2015). In accordance with this distinct developmental origin, previous work has shown that dLGN is composed of glutamatergic relay neurons, whereas IGL/LGv are almost entirely GABAergic and express transcription factors absent in dLGN, including Sox14 and Gata2 (Borghuis et al., 2014; Seabrook et al., 2017; delogu et al., 2012; Jager et al., 2021)
247159795_aeeef91c.section: Connectivity and circuit function of vLGN GABAergic neurons

247159795_0eefb318.text: .We observed complete overlap of GFP and tdTomato expression in the LGv and IGL (Fig. 1D), and no overlap in dLGN. This demonstrates that all cells of the LGv and IGL that are derived from the pTH-R also express Sox14 and are GABAergic
247159795_0eefb318.section: Connectivity and circuit function of vLGN GABAergic neurons

247159795_d79097dc.text: .LGv and IGL each consist of a dorsal region with a pTH-R thalamic origin and a ventral region composed of prethalamic cells (Jager et al., 2021). Thus, to clearly distinguish the developmental origin of these cells, we refer to cells in dorsal IGL/LGv as Sox14+ neurons
247159795_d79097dc.section: Connectivity and circuit function of vLGN GABAergic neurons

247159795_61ac7818.text: .Sox14+ neurons in ventral LGv and IGL exhibit projection neuron morphology: sparse local arborization with a main projection extending ventrally (Fig. 1E–G)
247159795_61ac7818.section: Connectivity and circuit function of vLGN GABAergic neurons

247159795_9ed56c01.text: .We find that Sox14+ neurons of the IGL/LGv project heavily to many visual and nonvisual targets (Fig. 2), including the superior colliculus, pretectum, and several nuclei known to regulate circadian rhythms, arousal and sleep (Fig. 2A–C), consistent with previous tracing studies in rat and hamster (Harrington, 1997; Morin and Blanchard, 2001; Morin and Allen, 2006)
247159795_9ed56c01.section: Connectivity and circuit function of vLGN GABAergic neurons

247159795_f4eefc59.text: .We observed projection overlap with reported broad viral labeling of IGL/LGv projections in superior colliculus, pretectal nuclei, olivary pretectal nucleus, vestibular nuclei, and zona incerta (Morin and Blanchard, 2001; Morin and Allen, 2006; Seabrook et al., 2017). We also observed dense fibers in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, subparaventricular zone, and ventrolateral preoptic area, and a sparse projection to the lateral habenula, all of which have not been previously reported

247159795_fe42d942.text: Hence, the mature IGL and LGv are characterized by a heterogenous cellular composition that includes Sox14 1 GABAergic thalamic neurons.

247159795_aaf65bdf.text: Notably, dense innervation was seen in the superficial gray and optic layers of the superior colliculus (SCs; Fig. 1M), while few immunoreactive fibers were present at the ventral edge of the SCN (Fig. 1N)

247159795_806081b0.text: GABAergic projection neurons are present at the rostroventral edges of the mouse thalamus to form the intergeniculate leaflet (IGL; Morin and Blanchard, 1999, 2001, 2005).

247159795_543a9ee7.text: While the Sox14 1 neurons constitute a thalamic cell class prominently found in the IGL, they also contribute to the prethalamic LGv nucleus.
